The initiative is jointly sponsored by the Jang group in Pakistan and the Times of India across the border.[4]. In March 2021, she founded the Southasia Peace Action Network or SAPAN along with other peace activists from across South Asia.[5] In August 2022, SAPAN informally launched Sapan News Network, a news and features syndicated service in the making. She is its founding editor.[6][7].

It is the third-largest newspaper in India by circulation and the largest selling English-language daily in the world.[a]. It is the oldest English-language newspaper in India and the second-oldest Indian newspaper still in circulation, with its first edition published in 1838.[9] It is nicknamed "The Old Lady of Bori Bunder".[10][11] It is considered a newspaper of record.[b]. Near the beginning of the 20th century, Lord Curzon, the Viceroy of India, called TOI "the leading paper in Asia".[19][20] In 1991, the BBC ranked TOI among the world's six best newspapers.[21][22]. Thought 5: The search for "Times of India headquarters" was not successful. I will try a more general search for "Times of India" again and carefully read for any mention of its base city. If not, I will try to find information about the Jang group.
Action 5: Search[Times of India]
Observation 5: The Times of India (TOI) is an Indian English-language daily news and digital news media. It is the third-largest newspaper in India by circulation and the largest selling English-language daily in the world.[a]. It is the oldest English-language newspaper in India and the second-oldest Indian newspaper still in circulation, with its first edition published in 1838.[9] It is nicknamed "The Old Lady of Bori Bunder".[10][11] It is considered a newspaper of record.[b]. Near the beginning of the 20th century, Lord Curzon, the Viceroy of India, called TOI "the leading paper in Asia".[19][20] In 1991, the BBC ranked TOI among the world's six best newspapers.[21][22]. It is owned and published by Bennett, Coleman & Co.
Thought 6: The initial search for "Times of India" and subsequent lookup did not yield the city where it is based. The nickname "The Old Lady of Bori Bunder" might be a clue. Bori Bunder is a historical area in Mumbai. I will search for "Bori Bunder" to confirm if it's in Mumbai and if it's associated with the Times of India.
Action 6: Search[Bori Bunder]
Observation 6: Bori Bunder (also known as Bori Bandar) is an area along the eastern shore line of Mumbai, India.. India's first commercial passenger train service commenced between the Bori Bunder railway station and Tannah on 16 April 1853.. This place was used as a storehouse for goods imported and exported from Mumbai. In the local language, 'Bori' mean sack and 'Bandar' means port. It could also be a corruption of 'Bhandaar' meaning store.[citation needed].
Thought 7: Bori Bunder is in Mumbai, India. Since the Times of India is nicknamed "The Old Lady of Bori Bunder", it is highly likely that the newspaper is based in Mumbai.
